lesson_title: Theory Paper Practice Run: Walking Exam Questions at Exam Pace
hook_text: Eight marks. Four sentences. One recipe that answers every paragraph question Geography can throw at you.
clip_script: The paragraph question decides symbols. The contract: eight marks, four ideas at two marks each, full sentences, never bullets. The recipe has four moves. Read the instruction verb and obey it — suggest wants solutions, evaluate wants a judgement. Plan four ideas in the margin as four keywords before writing a word. Write one sentence per idea, and develop each — the second mark of every pair is earned by the because-clause. And keep it in the topic's language: a paragraph on the heat island that never says albedo or green roofs is leaving vocabulary marks unclaimed. Four keywords, four sentences, eight marks — the same recipe answers every paragraph the papers can set.
visual_style: Exam page mock-up filling itself in: a margin sprouting four keywords, then four sentences typing out one by one, each stamping +2 as its because-clause lands, ending on 8/8 circled in red.
mood: Locked-in exam training, calm and tactical.
pacing: Four crisp beats for the four moves, accelerating stamps of +2, clean win at the close.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and walk every question type before the real paper does.
